title: Adaptive throttle & queue triage playbook for hosted GPU exhaustion
creator: Marco Chen
description: This ticket captures follow-up work from the 2026-02-25 hosted API GPU capacity exhaustion event. The incident manifested as prolonged queue buildup on multiple GPU pools, tenant-level throttling, and cascading request timeouts for low-latency chat endpoints. We observed a blend of workload shape (high fanout of short-sequence requests), autoscaler cooldown/hysteresis that delayed capacity recovery, and admission logic that amplified queue lengths for lower-priority tenants. The goal of this work is to deliver a reproducible playbook and a set of code/config changes that reduce likelihood of similar incidents and reduce MTTR when they occur.
timeline: 2026-02-25: Spike observed 04:12 UTC; 04:18 UTC: SLO breaches and increased 5xx; 04:30 UTC: incident declared; 05:10 UTC: emergency throttle & temporary tenant caps applied; 05:45 UTC: manual pool priming started; 07:00 UTC: sustained throughput recovered; 2026-02-26: initial RCA meeting; 2026-02-28: engineering follow-up scoped; 2026-03-03: prototype admission scoring landed in canary; 2026-03-08: playbook draft reviewed by SRE and PM; 2026-03-10: incremental rollout of adaptive throttle experiment started.
root_cause: The immediate trigger was a sudden increase in small, low-duration chat generation requests from a handful of tenants with aggressive retry/parallelization patterns. Autoscaler cooldown and preemption policies prevented timely GPU priming for the burst shape, while the admission controller's per-connection fairness logic favored long-running requests and allowed short requests to queue and amplify. Additionally, KV cache miss rate on newly primed replicas increased per-token compute, worsening utilization. A secondary factor was insufficient backpressure signals from downstream media proxies, delaying ingress shedding upstream.
decision: Adopt a multi-pronged mitigation: (1) implement adaptive, token-weighted admission credits per tenant to prevent queue amplification; (2) introduce a triage playbook for on-call to rapidly classify bursts (cold-start vs sustained) and execute targeted prewarm or tenant caps; (3) shorten autoscaler cooldown for rapid, short-lived bursts and add opportunistic prewarm paths; (4) add prefix cache warming heuristics during prewarm; (5) formalize staged shedding policies (soft shed then hard caps) with tenant-exposed signals.
